catalogue_metadata.scope_notes: Extraction focused on non-agentic structural, domain, and data-flow patterns across Python runner modules, governance actions, dashboard models, and knowledge base structures.
analysis_limits: Repository inspected via AST metadata, directory structures, and key file symbol tables without complete full-text file inspection of internal rule contents.

system_map.overview: cas_runner is a continuous architecture governance framework composed of a CLI entry point, domain-specific governance action and compliance engines, runtime flow orchestrators, and a file-backed knowledge repository (cas-knowledge).

layers.name: presentation-cli
layers.purpose: Provides user-facing command-line execution interfaces and workspace initialization entrypoints.

layers.name: application-orchestration
layers.purpose: Coordinates pipeline flow runs, health diagnostics, and governance lifecycle dispatching.

layers.name: domain-governance-steering
layers.purpose: Encapsulates continuous architecture domain models, transition state registries, compliance engines, and capability records.

layers.name: infrastructure-clients
layers.purpose: Provides external client wrappers, LLM abstraction adapters, and file system / telemetry integrations.

components.name: FlowRunner
components.responsibility: Executes sequential operational tasks and governance checks across architectural stages.

components.name: GovernanceActionEngine & TransitionRegistry
components.responsibility: Registers governance state transitions and validates operational actions against compliance requirements.

components.name: ComplianceEngine
components.responsibility: Calculates health metrics and compliance findings over architectural artifacts.

components.name: HealthModel
components.responsibility: Aggregates traceable health metrics and determines operational status.

orchestration.flow: CLI -> FlowRunner -> GovernanceActionService -> GovernanceActionEngine -> ComplianceEngine / Knowledge Artifacts

tools_and_integrations.role: Strict schema validation and data serialization for domain models
Distributed tracing and telemetry integration across runner flows
Structural schema validation of runtime rules and templates

state_and_memory.type: File-system backed structured knowledge base (JSON, YAML, Markdown ADRs)

patterns.name: Pydantic-Backed Typed Domain Entity Modeling
patterns.summary: Core continuous architecture entities, metrics, and actions are implemented as immutable/strongly-typed Pydantic models to guarantee invariant checking and boundary validation across layers.
patterns.intent: Ensure that runtime governance entities such as GovernanceInventory, ComplianceMetrics, and CapabilityRecord are structurally valid and self-describing across execution stages.
patterns.context: Architectural governance consumes and produces heterogeneous schema data across file systems, CLI commands, and automated checks.
forces: Loose JSON/YAML dictionaries cause runtime KeyError failures
Validation logic must remain coupled to entity definitions without polluting orchestration code
patterns.solution: Define data structures as specialized Pydantic models with typed attributes and schema constraints within dedicated models modules.
implementation_signals: Presence of strongly-typed records: ResolutionResult, TraceableMetric, ComplianceFinding, CapabilityRecord

evidence.note: Defines core typed models for governance state, action results, and compliance metrics
Models capability hierarchies and architectural deltas with explicit structural models

benefits: Eliminates silent data corruption across pipeline stages
Generates unambiguous JSON schema contracts for external consumption
costs: Runtime serialization/parsing overhead on dense file traversals
failure_modes: Schema changes without migration paths can break persisted knowledge files

patterns.reuse_notes: Extract domain models into standalone validation libraries for consumption by peripheral CI/CD tools.

patterns.name: Transition Registry State Machine Pattern
patterns.summary: Decouples lifecycle state transition definitions from execution engines by using an explicit registry that determines allowed transitions and validation gates.
patterns.intent: Maintain deterministic architectural transition paths (e.g. proposed -> accepted -> superseded) without embedding monolithic conditional trees inside service classes.
patterns.context: Architectural governance decisions progress through multi-stage lifecycles that require compliance and validation hooks at each step.
forces: Hard-coded if/else state machines become brittle as new governance stages are introduced
Action executions need decoupled pre-condition validations
patterns.solution: Use a TransitionRegistry class to register allowed states, target transitions, and pre-transition checks, which are queried by the GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: GovernanceAction model encapsulating transition request metadata

evidence.note: Encapsulates transition lookups and execution within a dedicated state engine

benefits: Extensible lifecycle states can be registered dynamically
Separates state transition rules from persistence or presentation
costs: Requires upfront configuration of registries before action execution
failure_modes: Unregistered states can result in abrupt rejection of valid transitions if registry is misconfigured

patterns.name: Layered Service-Engine Architectural Separation
patterns.summary: Splits business governance logic into a Service facade coordinating workflows and an Engine implementing core mathematical and policy calculations.
patterns.intent: Separate external invocation, orchestration, and parameter handling from underlying business compliance computation.
patterns.context: The runner needs to execute governance operations from CLI commands or CI workflows while keeping core calculation logic pure and testable.
forces: Coupling service orchestration with low-level metric math hinders unit testability
Engines should not be concerned with workspace bootstrap or CLI parameter parsing
patterns.solution: Implement GovernanceActionService as the coordination boundary while delegating pure rule computation and evaluation to ComplianceEngine and GovernanceActionEngine.
implementation_signals: Service calls engines passing domain models

evidence.note: Serves as orchestration boundary for governance actions
Performs pure compliance rule verification and metric aggregation

benefits: High testability of engine logic without mocking service infrastructure
Clear boundary for CLI and runner orchestrators
costs: Additional indirection layer between runner triggers and calculation
failure_modes: Risk of anemic service anti-pattern if service simply delegates 1:1 without value-add orchestration

patterns.name: File-Backed Knowledge Repository and Template Strategy
patterns.summary: Stores organizational architectural decisions, governance rules, and signals in a version-controlled directory tree structured by scope (global vs project).
patterns.intent: Treat architecture documents, signals, rules, and decisions as first-class, Git-versioned assets rather than storing them in external opaque databases.
patterns.context: Continuous architecture relies on PR reviews, Git tracking, and transparent traceability of architecture evolution.
forces: External databases disconnect architectural documentation from code commits
Human and automated agents must be able to read and modify architectural artifacts uniformly
patterns.solution: Organize artifacts under `cas-knowledge/` divided into `global/`, `governance/`, `projects/`, and `templates/` using standard Markdown and YAML formats.
implementation_signals: Templates for adrs, decisions, heuristics, signals, and rules
Workspace bootstrap logic ensuring structure presence

evidence.note: Standardized ADR template for GitOps governance
Scaffolds and validates knowledge directory layout

benefits: Native auditability and branch-based approvals via Git
Standardized markdown templates enforce consistent record authoring
costs: File system querying and parsing can suffer performance bottlenecks at scale
failure_modes: Manual human file edits can introduce schema parsing errors if not validated in pre-commit

patterns.name: Health Status Metric Aggregation Heuristic
patterns.summary: Evaluates architectural repository health via composite functional evaluation over compliance findings, yielding deterministic qualitative status states.
patterns.intent: Translate granular quantitative compliance findings and metrics into actionable health statuses (e.g. HEALTHY, DEGRADED, UNHEALTHY).
patterns.context: Dashboard and CI/CD pipelines need a unified status indicator to block or permit pull requests and pipeline runs.
forces: Raw metrics are too fine-grained for binary or tri-state CI gate decisions
Explanations must be provided alongside binary green/red statuses
patterns.solution: Encapsulate health calculation within pure utility functions that compute HealthStatus and provide human-readable reason lists.

evidence.note: Aggregates compliance findings into health status classifications

benefits: Clear traceability between high-level health flags and root-cause compliance findings
costs: Fixed threshold heuristics may require manual tuning per organization
failure_modes: Misweighted findings may result in false alarms or undetected architectural drift

patterns.name: Pluggable External Client Adapter with Test Double
patterns.summary: Maintains production and mock implementations conforming to identical interfaces to decouple high-cost infrastructure integrations from unit tests and offline workflows.
patterns.intent: Enable running runner governance and synthesis steps offline and during deterministic unit tests without calling external endpoints.
patterns.context: External model clients (LiteLLM) introduce network dependencies and nondeterminism into testing pipelines.
forces: CI pipelines must run quickly and deterministically without external credentials
Production runtime requires real remote API invocation
patterns.solution: Provide parallel client implementations (LiteLLMClient vs MockLLMClient) exposing identical execution signatures.
implementation_signals: LiteLLMClient and MockLLMClient placed in the same module namespace

evidence.note: In-memory test double for zero-dependency execution

benefits: Simplified local development and dry-run execution
costs: Risk of drift between MockLLMClient behavior and live remote API contracts
failure_modes: Mock client returning outdated response schemas

anti_patterns.name: Monolithic Direct File-System Coupling in Engines
symptoms: Engines and services reading and parsing raw JSON/YAML directly from disk paths rather than going through an abstract repository interface
impact: Tightly couples business rule calculation to local path layouts
Complicates testing by forcing creation of temporary files on disk
suggested_remediation: Introduce a formal Repository interface (e.g., KnowledgeRepository protocol) that encapsulates disk reading and schema parsing away from domain engines.

anti_patterns.name: Bifurcated Model Hierarchy Drift
symptoms: Governance models and steering models defined separately in distinct packages (governance/models.py and steering/models.py) with overlapping architectural delta concepts
impact: Requires translation bridges between governance verification and steering projection
Risk of inconsistent entity definitions for identical domain concepts (e.g. changes, actions)
suggested_remediation: Consolidate core shared entities into a common domain kernel module to prevent dual definitions of ArchitecturalDelta and GovernanceAction.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: OpenTelemetry Observability
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Integration of opentelemetry-api and opentelemetry-sdk across runner workflows to record traces for compliance checks, steering sync, and transitions.

cross_cutting_concerns.name: Static Code Quality and Lint Standards
cross_cutting_concerns.description: Repo-wide enforcement of PEP8, pyupgrade, flake8, and import sorting via Ruff with explicit line length and rule selection.

open_questions.detail: Will cas_runner introduce a database or remote object store backend for large enterprise deployments, or will Git-backed file trees remain the sole persistence mechanism?
How does ComplianceEngine enforce isolation when evaluating custom dynamic rule scripts to prevent arbitrary code execution on developer machines?
